So the February window is a deferred matrícula for the autumn-admitted, not a second cohort with its own application — it fails the brief's test («an application window that merely opens in spring» does not count; nor does a matrícula window with no admission behind it). notes: UIB has the most elaborate ladder of late-entry routes found in this slice — four of them, ending in an open-ended individual out-of-deadline process — and NONE of them is a spring intake. They are strictly sequential fill-ups of the same September cohort: the September convocatòria's own lists and matrícula land in October, after teaching has begun. UIB itself says so in a warning that is directly on point for this candidate: «És recomanable que els estudiants estrangers participin a les convocatòries d'admissió de juny i juliol per tenir més temps per tramitar el visat abans de l'inici de l'any acadèmic atès que la publicació de les llistes d'admesos i la matrícula de la convocatòria de setembre és al mes d'octubre.» A non-EU applicant should therefore treat the June/July rounds as the only realistic ones at UIB. One caveat worth a human check: UIB sets no central master's teaching calendar — each master's direction reports its own start and end dates to the CEP — so an individual UIB master could in principle run an off-cycle calendar without it showing in any central document. Nothing found suggests one does, but the negative here rests on the admission calendar, which is central, rather than on a central teaching calendar, which does not exist.
